title: Ruined Castle Courtyard
name: scene_ruined_castle
scene_summary: The inner courtyard of a castle ruined long ago, seen from above: one open yard of cracked flagstones with grass growing through the joints, ringed by broken walls, with a well at its centre.
render_details: Cracked grey flagstones with grass in the joints and whole slabs fallen away, tumbled masonry blocks, dry leaves drifted into corners, a mossy round well head, splintered crates, rusted weapons lying about, ivy on the broken stonework

rooms.label: Inner Courtyard
rooms.description: One open courtyard of cracked flagstones with grass growing through the joints and several patches fallen away into bare earth. It is one continuous open yard: nothing is built on it, and the only walls are the ruined ones around its edge.

annotations.label: The Well
annotations.description: A round stone well head standing alone in the middle of the courtyard, its low wall thick with moss, its mouth open and black, with splintered crates and a few rusted weapons lying on the flagstones around it

annotations.label: Collapsed North Wall
annotations.description: A length of curtain wall whose upper courses have fallen, leaving a jagged broken edge and several great masonry blocks lying in a heap at its foot, high enough to climb and stand on

annotations.label: Watch Tower
annotations.description: The lower storey of a round watch tower, opened to the sky, its upper floors gone, one gap in the ring of its wall opening to the courtyard, a stone spiral stair inside it winding up along the wall and seen from directly above as a ring of wedge-shaped treads

annotations.label: Ruined Colonnade
annotations.description: A row of thick stone columns left standing from a covered walk that has otherwise fallen, each column a separate block of stone with floor visible all round it and clear gaps between them, the covering they carried gone entirely

annotations.label: Iron Gates
annotations.description: A pair of great rusted iron gates in the far wall, standing ajar with a gap between them, nothing but flat darkness visible through the opening
